title: Spiritual Freedom
english: We have been freed from blemish and justified through our faith in him, and through this faith, we have been enriched with the safety and protection that come from him, and we have been fortified with his grace, which repels every diabolical attack and the fierce rebellions of opposing powers.

This is a lesson that is taught to us as if we were being addressed as the Church of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, where it will no longer be possible for the uncircumcised and unclean to pass through.

Historically, the nations surrounding Jerusalem, which were uncircumcised and unclean, did not know God by nature and truth, nor had they received the pedagogy of the law, and they often fought against those of the blood of Israel, seeming to be stronger than the power residing in them, and trampling it underfoot.

However, when we interpret spiritual things from historical events, we see that the ranks of demons, the rulers of this darkness, and the profane Satan have underfoot the souls not yet generated by God, passing through them with no one hindering or defending, but when these souls have been glorified and strengthened by God, then the greed of those demonic powers will cease.
For it is written that an angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear Him and rescue them (Psalm 34:7).
The abominable and unclean things are to be considered defiled and wicked, and they are contrary to God's power.
To Jerusalem, the Lord says, 'Shake off the dust, rise, and sit,' and to the captive daughter of Zion, 'Remove the bond from your neck' (Isaiah 52:2).
Then the Lord teaches clearly how she will put on the strength of her arm and the glory.

The dust that the Lord commands to be shaken off is not just physical dust, but also the earthly mindset and the uncleanness of carnal desires that cling to us, so we must shake off the dust, and this means removing the earthly mindset and cleansing our mind.

Just as those who lie on the ground are filled with dust and dirt, so also those who have an earthly mindset are filled with the uncleanness of carnal desires, and therefore, we who are called to spiritual intimacy with our Lord Jesus Christ and are about to put Him on as strength and glory must first shake off the earthly mindset and cleanse our mind.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the beginning or end.
The translation aims to preserve the original word order and meaning as much as possible, while still conveying the author's intended message in natural literary prose.

title: Christ's Sacrifice
english: Christ's sacrifice has the power to sanctify the people through his own blood, because he suffered not for his own sake, but for the sake of all people under heaven.
The worship prescribed by the law was unable to remove sins on earth, since sacrifices and sheep slaughters were displeasing to God.
However, the true lamb, who takes away the sin of the world, offered himself as a fragrant odor for us.
As Paul testifies in writing, God did not spare his own Son, but handed him over for us all, so that with him he may grant us all things.

Christ himself says through the Psalmist, 'You did not want a sacrifice and offering, but a body you prepared for me; you did not approve whole burnt offerings and sin offerings; then I said, "Behold, I come"; it is written in the scroll of the book about me, to do your will, O God' (Psalm 40:6-8).
Having endured the death of the flesh, Christ freed the whole world under heaven from death and sin, because one who is worthy of all suffered for all, so that he may rule and reign over all.
Paul also writes that Christ died and lived, so that he may be Lord of both the dead and the living.
One person died on behalf of all, so that those who are living would no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died and rose for them.
The prophet describes this person as one who knows how to bear weaknesses, has his face set towards the afflicted, is despised, and not considered, and who bears our sins and suffers for us.

We thought he was in pain, affliction, and evil, because we believed the passion happened to him as a divine punishment for some sins, and that because of that sin, he was in pain, affliction, and evil.
But it is not so; rather, he was wounded because of our sins and weakened because of our lawlessness.
The prophetic word proceeds with simplicity, and the face of those not knowing the mystery of Christ is hypocritical, thinking that he became afflicted due to his own sins.
We thought he was in pain, affliction, and evil, that is, we thought the passion happened to him as a divine punishment for some sins, and because of that sin, he was in pain, affliction, and evil.
But it is not so; rather, he was wounded because of our sins and weakened because of our lawlessness.
Then he gives other reasons, through which it can be seen that the sinless one suffered for the sake of our salvation and life.
For we were formerly at enmity with God, fighting against his holy laws, not having the yoke of obedience, and refusing to serve him.
But it was necessary…
translator_notes: The Greek text ends mid-sentence with 'Ἀλλ' ἦν ἀναγκαῖο', so the final clause is rendered as 'But it was necessary…' to reflect the fragment.
The Greek word 'ἀνομίας' is translated as 'lawlessness' in the text, though it may also be rendered as 'iniquity' or 'wickedness'.

title: Condemnation of Idolatry
english: Those who call upon idols under thick trees are the ones who slaughter their children in the clefts among the rocks.
By calling them murderers, God shows that hatred of Him was a deep-seated weakness in them and that their readiness for bloodshed was not a new development, but rather a long-standing inherent trait.
You are the ones who, according to the times above, call upon idols under thick trees.

Although the law through Moses was given to them, saying, 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only' (Deuteronomy 6:13), they fell into madness, or rather, into impiety beyond all measure, as they became makers of idols and ministers to them.
They even taught others to worship under thick trees, crowning these idols with divine honors, which is a clear violation of God's commandments.

This is clearly established by God through the voice of Jeremiah, who said, 'You saw what the house of Israel did to me' (Jeremiah 3:6), describing how they went upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree and fornicated there.
They seized the mountain tops and the most beautiful parts of the groves, building altars and temples, and offering sacrifices and libations to the unclean demons.
Some even spared not their own children, as Jehonias slaughtered his own son to the non-existent gods.
God said through one of the holy prophets, 'Sacrifice humans, for calves are lacking' (Jeremiah 7:31).
You are the ones calling upon idols, slaughtering your children under dense trees in the ravines among the rocks.
On these things, therefore, shall I not be angry?
What then is your portion?
Your lot is that you have bowed down to vain things and will have a vain portion and lot.
You will be bound by equal evils and slaughter will be your portion and lot, because you became a child-killer and poured libations to unclean and lifeless demon idols, offering sacrifices to them.
translator_notes: The name 'Jehonias' is used, which may be a variant of the name 'Jehoiachin' or 'Jeconiah'.
The text begins mid-sentence: '...you have the one who brings into rhythm in piety through evangelical decrees.'
